issues.description: _shutdown_telemetry strips every LoggingHandler from the root logger, mutating global state and clobbering handlers this module did not install.
issues.detail: The shutdown path iterates the root logger and removes all opentelemetry LoggingHandler instances, including any installed by user code or other subsystems. Hold the handler reference returned by _setup_cloud_tracer and remove only that one. Global mutation to fix a local re-entrant-emit deadlock is the wrong scope.

issues.description: _flush_early_log_buffer locates the OTLP handler by isinstance scan over root.handlers and silently no-ops or replays into the wrong sink.
issues.detail: The replay path picks the first LoggingHandler in root.handlers. If another subsystem installed one first, it eats the replay; if none exists, the fix the PR claims to ship silently does nothing. Keep a direct reference to the handler created in _setup_cloud_tracer and address it by identity, not by type scan.

issues.description: _BufferingHandler.buffer is an unbounded list[LogRecord] with no cap, drop policy, or time bound.
issues.detail: Between _start_log_buffering and flush or cleanup, the buffer grows without limit. A slow-hanging job or a chatty DEBUG library can balloon memory before the worker notices. Make it a bounded ring (size or bytes) with an explicit drop policy; a crash-log feature that can OOM the worker is worse than the bug it fixes.

issues.description: Crash-log path complects buffering, recording-policy decisions, and handler discovery across JobContext and telemetry.
issues.detail: _on_cleanup synthesizes RecordingOptions with logs=True regardless of user/server config, then re-enters init_recording with unreasoned interaction against prior _recording_initialized state. Separate the buffer (value), the upload-on-crash policy, and the handler identity so each can be reasoned about and tested independently.

issues.description: _on_entry_done forces _shutdown_fut on crash, overloading one future with two distinct postconditions.
issues.detail: Resolving _shutdown_fut with reason='job crashed' from a done-callback conflates orderly user/timeout shutdown with task failure. Downstream consumers branching on shutdown_info now see broadened semantics. Use a typed reason (CRASH vs USER vs TIMEOUT) or a separate signal; do not smuggle crash control flow through a future meant for orderly shutdown.

issues.description: Patch bundles unrelated worker.py race fix, makefile pytest-xdist removal, and test_plugin_google_stt drop with the crash-log feature.
issues.detail: Reordering _pending_assignments before _queue_msg is a real race fix; dropping -n auto serializes CI for everyone; removing test_plugin_google_stt looks like a local workaround. None is motivated by the PR description. Split into separate commits so bisect, revert, and review work; justify the makefile change or quarantine the flaky test instead.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the intent is right — buffering early logs and force-resolving shutdown so crash logs reach the server is the correct shape — but the implementation has two serious scoping bugs and several smaller hygiene problems. Both shutdown handler removal and replay-path handler discovery use isinstance scans over the global root logger, which can clobber unrelated handlers and silently route replays to the wrong sink; hold the handler by reference instead. The in-memory buffer is unbounded, the crash-log path complects buffering with recording policy and handler discovery, and _shutdown_fut is overloaded to carry crash semantics. Finally, three unrelated changes (worker.py race fix, makefile -n auto removal, test_plugin_google_stt drop) are bundled without justification and should travel separately. NEEDS-WORK before landing.
